strings.name: Steve Wozniak
strings.summary: Steve Wozniak designed the core hardware and software of the Apple I and Apple II and co-founded Apple with Steve Jobs, helping broaden the market for personal computers. His engineering achieved useful functions with economical designs. After leaving day-to-day company work, he pursued ventures, philanthropy and technology education, connecting hobbyist electronics, product design and hands-on learning.
strings.coverageNote: Research checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2026. This is not a daily news archive. Shared achievements are credited to collaborators and teams.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Apple and designed early personal computers, helping move computing devices from laboratories into the mass market.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: UC Berkeley bachelor's in electrical engineering and computer sciences (1986)
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Early Apple computers
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Designed the Apple I and Apple II, combining practical hardware and software with keyboard and display interfaces.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Hands-on technology education
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Contributed time and resources to school equipment, teacher support and practical learning for children.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Engineering reflections at Lehigh
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Discussed early personal-computer design, engineering interests and AI in a public university conversation.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Inventors Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Inducted for contributions to personal-computer design.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Completed Berkeley degree
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Finished his remaining coursework and earned an electrical engineering and computer-science degree.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: National Medal of Technology
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Received the US medal with Jobs for contributions to personal computing.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Returned to university
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Took time away from Apple following an airplane accident and resumed studies at Berkeley.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Apple II introduced
strings.timeline.event-6.text: His Apple II brought color graphics and an expandable design to home and school computing.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Co-founded Apple
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Founded Apple with Jobs and partners, turning the Apple I hobbyist design into a commercial product.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Developed Apple I
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Designed a personal computer using a keyboard and display and shared his work with hobbyists.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in San Jose
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Born in San Jose, California, and developed an early interest in electronics.
